description:
After a short break, we resumed our journey along the ancient Silk Road, delving into the heart of Iran, one of the most misunderstood countries in the world. Our first stop was Mashhad, Iran’s holiest and most conservative city. Renowned for its religious significance, Mashhad is a sacred destination for Shia Muslims, housing the revered Imam Reza Holy Shrine.
The city itself is stunning, offering a blend of rich history, breathtaking architecture, and vibrant culture. What stood out the most, however, were the incredibly warm and hospitable locals who made our visit even more memorable. Historically, Mashhad was also a key stop on the ancient Silk Road, connecting the Iranian plateau to Merv to the east, serving as an important trading and cultural hub for centuries.
Join me on this adventure through the ancient Persia 🎬
